cases.statement: One person: Patient 4 of a nine-patient retrospective series from one centre; infantile onset (10 months). Sex not stated for this patient.

people.label: Patient 4
people.other_allele: not applicable (dominant); the same person also carries a second GFAP variant, c.170C>T (p.Ala57Val), also found in the healthy father
people.key_phenotypes: hypotonia with onset at 10 months; seizures from 3.5 years; macrocephaly; failure to thrive and dysphagia needing a G-tube; spastic ataxic gait from 10 years; typical radiologic features

| general information | general information | age at first symptoms | 4m | 6m | 4m | 10m | 7m | 1y | 46y | 12y | 2y/6y |
These three variants were all present in a heterozygous state.
Patient 4 was described as a “bad eater” and presented with hypotonia but an otherwise normal motor development until the age of ten months.
At the age of ten years a spastic ataxic gait disorder appeared.

In addition to the motor delay, the patient presented with seizures (first one at the age of three and a half years), macrocephaly, failure to thrive, paroxysmal deterioration, dysphasia, slow speech, and dysphagia, leading to the necessity of a G-Tube.
Typical radiologic features were found.

phenotype_specificity.statement: Authors describe typical radiologic features and an infantile course (seizures, macrocephaly, bulbar signs). No testing of other genes is described for this patient; the testing method is not stated.

quotes.quote: Typical radiologic features were found.

In addition to the motor delay, the patient presented with seizures (first one at the age of three and a half years), macrocephaly, failure to thrive, paroxysmal deterioration, dysphasia, slow speech, and dysphagia, leading to the necessity of a G-Tube.

Retrospective data from nine patients of the Hamburg leukodystrophy centre with a confirmed diagnosis of AxD, either by identification of a pathogenic variant GFAP or detection of Rosenthal fibres in autopsy, were analyzed.

segregation.statement: No relative is reported as tested for c.1118A>G. The healthy father carries the second variant c.170C>T; his status for c.1118A>G is not stated explicitly.

quotes.quote: In addition to the pathogenic variant c.1118A>G, patient 4 also carried another rare variant (c.170C>T, p.Ala57Val).
As this variant was also present in the patient’s healthy father, we classified this variant as likely non-pathogenic.

de_novo.statement: Authors state that two of the three novel variants arose de novo; by exclusion of c.209G>C (patient 7) these are c.1118A>G and c.1013T>C, and the authors' criteria list for c.1118A>G includes the de novo criterion. Which parents were tested, by what method, and whether parentage was confirmed are not reported.

quotes.quote: Two of these variants arose de novo, while for the third (c.209G>C, patient 7), no segregation data was available.

According to ACMG guidelines, the variants c.1118A>G (PM1, PP2, PM2, PM5, PP3, PS2) and c.1013T>C (PM1, PP2, PM2, PP3, PS2) were classified as pathogenic variants, while the variant c.209G>C was classified as likely pathogenic (PM1, PP2, PM2, PM5, PP3) [30].

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Missense, p.(Glu373Gly), exon 6 per the paper. Authors state the variant lies in a mutational hotspot region and that disease variants mostly act by gain of function. A different nucleotide change at the same codon (c.1118A>C, p.Glu373Ala) is listed in another batch paper's review table.

quotes.quote: We identified three GFAP gene variants, which had not been published to date: c.1118A>G (p.Glu373Gly) and c.1013T>C (p.Leu338Pro), both in exon 6, (the latter is described by A. Messing as an unpublished variant, without neuropathological confirmation [27]), and c.209G>C (p.Arg70Pro) in exon 1.
They were predicted to be non-truncating on the protein level but leading to non-synonymous amino acids alteration located in mutational hotspot regions [30].
The pathogenic gene variants are in most cases de novo missense variants, leading to a gain of function.

authors_classification.statement: Authors' ACMG call, made with the Franklin (Qiagen/Genoox) tool, quoted below.

quotes.quote: According to ACMG guidelines, the variants c.1118A>G (PM1, PP2, PM2, PM5, PP3, PS2) and c.1013T>C (PM1, PP2, PM2, PP3, PS2) were classified as pathogenic variants, while the variant c.209G>C was classified as likely pathogenic (PM1, PP2, PM2, PM5, PP3) [30].
Novel GFAP variants were classified according to the recommendations of the ACMG by using Franklin by Qiagen/Genoox [29,30].

concerns: Second GFAP variant in the same person: c.170C>T (p.Ala57Val), inherited from the healthy father; authors set it aside.

The de novo statement does not name the variants explicitly (only by exclusion of c.209G>C) and gives no details of parental testing or parentage confirmation; the father was tested at least for c.170C>T.
Criteria were assigned with an automated tool (Franklin), not by the authors' own stated reasoning.
Transcript not stated in the paper; sex of Patient 4 not stated.
No named in-silico tools or scores and no population data are reported beyond the criteria list.
notes_for_panel: Single case from a 2025 retrospective series. Phenotype is infantile-onset and reported as radiologically typical. Evidence for de novo occurrence rests on one summary sentence.
